title: Isothrum runner event, version 0
description:
One event of the stream.

Every event of an operation has `run` and `op`. An event written outside one ([`Event::new`])
has those its writer knows. The command line's own: a command line it refused has neither;
`reap`'s closing `result` and `error` have neither; any other failure before an operation
began has `op` when the command is an operation, and `run` when `--name` named it (a failure
of `status`, `console`, `events` or `key` has no `op`).

seq.description: Its place in the operation, from 1.

run.description:
The run's name: on every event of an operation; outside one, when its writer knows it
(see [`Event`]).

op.description:
The operation: on every event of an operation; outside one, when its writer knows it (see
[`Event`]).

oneOf.description: The run moved from one state to another.
A step started, finished, failed or was skipped.

note.description:
What it does, said when it starts: the manifest's line for a manifest step, the
runner's own for a step of its own (the tool probes, the boot, a guest delivery).

oneOf.description: A line a step's tool printed.

line.description: The line, without its line break.

oneOf.description: A ready condition was checked.
An output's value, once the run is up.

value.description: Its value (`***` when sensitive), or null when it can't be read.

oneOf.description: One check's result.

detail.description: Why it failed (empty when it passed).

oneOf.description: Something the embedder may show, that didn't fail the operation.
The operation's outcome, when it ran to its end.

ok.description: Whether it reached its goal (false: a check failed).

oneOf.description: Why the operation failed.

step.description: The step that failed, when one did.

timeout.description: Which limit the step ran into, when the code is `timeout`.

Its standard error.
Not yet; polled again.

An address.

WarningCode.description: What kind of warning a `warning` event is, the same in the Rust API and the event stream.

oneOf.description: A step whose failure the manifest tolerates failed.
A check runner failed or ran out of time: its checks that didn't report fail.

A clean-up of the checks failed: a check runner's that ran out of time (`on_timeout`), or
the teardown after a setup that failed too (the check ends with the setup's error).
What an earlier run left is removed before a start.
A VM (or its folder) an earlier run left was removed.
The run last ran on another Vagrant provider: that run is cleared first.
A VM's saved state was cut off: it boots fresh.
A start failed on stale state: cleared, then started again.

A step is tried again: an apply that failed, an `ssh.run` whose host doesn't answer yet, or a
Vagrant command another Vagrant process's lock on a machine refused.

An operation that failed couldn't update the run's record either: the operation's own
error is the one it ends with.

An output's `format` couldn't be filled (it names a value the run doesn't have): the
output has no value.

A resource a destroy found already gone (its provider's error, which the manifest names) is
dropped from the run's state, and the destroy runs again.

A clean-up the runner does on its own, best effort, failed (an earlier run's VM or its
folder, the hypervisor's list of them, the run on another Vagrant provider): what it would have removed may still be
there, and the start goes on.

ErrorCode.description: The stable code of a failure, the same in the Rust API and the event stream (`error.code`).

oneOf.description:
The manifest isn't valid JSON or breaks the contract, a value it gives can't be used as
written (a step's `verdict` that isn't a regular expression, an SSH login, a `wait_s`, a
`tcp` condition's port), or it names a value the operation doesn't have (a placeholder
with none, a guest delivery's machine whose address no output gives, a Terraform module
with no `.tf` file).
The manifest is another version of the contract.

The manifest needs something this runner doesn't do (a target that doesn't run on this
host, a delivery its driver doesn't take, an action of another driver's, a step with no
command for this host), or the call asks the run for something its target can't do (a
console into a Compose service with no VM, a Vagrant VM joined to another network).
A file or folder couldn't be read or written, or a socket on this computer bound.
Another process runs an operation on this run, or holds the home's slot pick.
A tool a step runs isn't installed.
A step's tool ran and failed.
A tool answers at a version older than the run needs.

A step showed no progress for its time limit, or ran to the ceiling every step stops at,
and was stopped, with what it started (the `error` event's `timeout` says which).

A download (what a step needs, fetched in a phase of its own before it: a Compose start's
images, a Vagrant start's boxes; or a step the manifest marks a download) showed no
progress for as long as a download may, and was stopped.

A download couldn't be made: its tool failed (the message says why: a registry or a box
catalog refusing it, a name it doesn't know, the network).
The run is already up.
The run is recorded on another place (server or account) than the one asked for.
A host port the run publishes is taken.
The manifest has no park steps for that mode.
Nothing of the run, or not every one of its machines, is left to resume.
The run isn't up.
A ready condition didn't hold.
A required secret or input has no value.
A param is unknown, missing or holds a value it doesn't allow.
A run name that can't name a run.

The run's Vagrant provider is missing, unknown, not on this host, refused by the run, or
lacks its plugin.

The elevation Hyper-V's commands need couldn't be had or was lost: the permission prompt
declined or unanswered, the elevated session not started or ended before the operation
(the message says which).
A machine the run doesn't have.
The run has several machines the call could mean, and it named none.
A network the run doesn't have.
Every slot of the place is held by another run.
A deployment can't be taken over as a run.
A machine a step goes to over SSH never answered.
The run's seal failed: it is up, but not sealed, so not ready.

The operation was cut short before it ended (its future dropped: an embedder's cancel, the
command line's Ctrl-C or SIGTERM); the tools it started were asked to stop, and are ended
once they have, or 30 seconds later.

The embedder was asked for something that makes no sense (the command line: a run folder
with no manifest, a value missing or malformed), so no operation started.

The machine has no graphical console to reach: its target or provider gives none (the
error says why), it isn't running, or its hypervisor doesn't say where it is.

TimedOut.description:
Which limit a step ran into: a timeout's, also the `error` event's `timeout`.

A step's limit (its `timeout_s`) counts the time it shows no progress: progress is an output
line, on either stream, that isn't blank and isn't one of the last distinct lines it printed
(a stuck download repeating `Downloading 1.121GB` makes none). A step that prints nothing has
its limit from its start. A step that keeps making progress still stops at a ceiling: six
hours from its start, or its limit when that is longer.

oneOf.description: It showed no progress for its limit.

last_line.description:
The last line it printed (secrets masked, cut to 300 bytes); none when it printed
nothing.

oneOf.description: It was still making progress at the ceiling.

after_s.description: The ceiling, in seconds from the step's start.
